| **D0001** | 4B | 4B.1, 4B.2 | López Obrador led his competitors in vote-intention polls by a margin of 20–30 percentage points in the period immediately preceding the July 2018 presidential election (March 2018 sampling period; no runoff system in Mexico). | positive | `extracted HTML block 62` segments S00004–S00005 (narrowest: S00004 only) | direct fit: pre-election period immediately before the scored ruler-period | Poll-based; does not constitute verified electoral outcome; poll margin alone does not measure democratic quality |
| **D0002** | 5B | 5B.1, 5B.8 | The López Obrador campaign program (2018–2024) proposed "republican austerity" as a fiscal policy linking reduction of current state operating expenditures to reorientation of public resources toward investment, without raising any taxes and without issuing debt. | positive | `extracted HTML block 62` segment S00007 | direct fit: campaign program announced before December 1, 2018 inauguration | Policy proposal not yet enacted; stated without upturn/tax increase not independently verified |
| **D0003** | 5B | 5B.8, 5B.9 | The stated program included a gradual increase of the minimum wage to 171 pesos at the end of the six-year term and an increase of senior-citizen pensions to monthly payments of 1,500 pesos. | positive | `extracted HTML block 62` segment S00008 | direct fit: campaign commitment for the 2018–2024 term | Proposed policy; enactment and actual incidence not yet observable in this passage |
| **D0004** | 8B | 8B.1, 8B.2 | The stated program included the review and reversal as necessary of Peña Nieto's energy reform, and the increase of domestic gasoline supply to reduce imports and lower prices, requiring the commissioning of additional refineries. | positive | `extracted HTML block 62` segments S00009–S00011 | direct fit: policy program for 2018–2024 term | Proposed reversal; implementation not confirmed; refinery capacity timeline not specified |
| **D0005** | 3B | 3B.6, 3B.9 | The stated security approach included addressing the social causes of violence by combating poverty and elevating human development among vulnerable groups, and the gradual withdrawal of the Armed Forces from internal security missions while deploying a new National Guard, with the stated goal of "pacifying" Mexico within three years. | positive | `extracted HTML block 63` segments S00001–S00002 | direct fit: campaign security platform for 2018–2024 term | Goal statement; three-year timeline aspirational; no implementation evidence yet |
| **D0006** | 7B | 7B.8, 7B.9 | López Obrador pledged to combat corruption and former-president privileges by "doing justice without vengeance or hatred," explicitly stating he would not imprison Peña Nieto. | mixed | `extracted HTML block 63` segment S00012 (narrowest: S00012) | direct fit: campaign commitment for 2018–2024 term | Self-contradictory intent signal; enforcement mechanism unspecified; promise not independently corroborated |
| **D0007** | 2B | 2B.3, 2B.7 | The stated program sought with the United States cooperative and good-neighbor relations based on mutual respect, framed against the context of Trump's border wall, unilateral tariffs on Mexican metal exports, and forced renegotiation of NAFTA. | mixed | `extracted HTML block 63` segments S00004–S00005 | direct fit: stated foreign-policy posture for 2018–2024 term | Aspirational framing; no evidence of enacted bilateral agreements or treaty outcomes in this passage |
| **D0008** | 5B | 5B.1, 5B.2 | The governing platform described by the source characterized López Obrador's approach as pragmatic social democracy assuming orthodox free-market principles, macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, and peso floatation, combined with rejection of privatization and "foreignization" of strategic sectors and prioritization of national production. | mixed | `extracted HTML block 63` segment S00009 (narrowest: S00009) | direct fit: governing platform for 2018–2024 term | Characterization by the source; ideological self-description not equivalent to enacted policy; tension between stated market-orthodox and nationalist elements unresolved |
| **D0009** | 8B | 8B.1 | On December 1, 2018, López Obrador took office as president for a six-year term, with his coalition holding an absolute majority in both chambers of Congress, and publicly committed to "not betraying the people" while respecting "the established legal order." | positive | `extracted HTML block 6` segments S00007–S00008 | direct fit: inauguration and first formal acts, start of scored period | Self-commitment statement; no independent verification of subsequent compliance; institutional constraints not yet observable |
| **D0010** | 3B | 3B.6, 3B.9 | Days before the inauguration, López Obrador presented a National Peace and Security Plan including creation of a National Guard to replace the Army, and announced study of conditional amnesty for drug traffickers and decriminalization of soft-drug consumption. | mixed | `extracted HTML block 6` segments S00010–S00011 (narrowest: S00010–S00011) | direct fit: pre-inauguration policy announcement setting term agenda | Pre-inauguration announcement; no enacted legislation; conditional amnesty language signals partial criminal-justice approach to drug violence |
| **D0011** | 8B | 8B.3 | The source classifies López Obrador as the first Mexican president "clearly from the left," noting he relied on an absolute congressional majority to govern. | positive | `extracted HTML block 6` segment S00007 | direct fit: start of ruler-period (December 1, 2018) | Source characterization; ideological label does not measure policy output or institutional quality |
| **D0012** | 4B | 4B.7 | The campaign program included defense of Mexican migrants in the context of Trump's border wall and forced NAFTA renegotiation, seeking US cooperation based on mutual respect. | positive | `extracted HTML block 63` segments S00004–S00005 | direct fit: campaign platform for 2018–2024 term | Policy intention; no enacted bilateral agreement or measurable outcome in this passage |
| **D0013** | 6B | 6B.1, 6B.3 | The stated program included food self-sufficiency goals, offering local agricultural producers guaranteed prices, alongside attention to poverty and human development for vulnerable populations. | positive | `extracted HTML block 62` segment S00011 and `extracted HTML block 5` segment S00004 | direct fit: campaign social platform for 2018–2024 term | Proposed policy; enacted implementation and actual incidence on vulnerable groups not yet observable |
| **D0014** | 5B | 5B.3 | The governing platform accepted the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico and peso floatation as structural commitments, alongside budget discipline and macroeconomic stability. | positive | `extracted HTML block 63` segment S00009 | direct fit: stated economic framework for 2018–2024 term | Policy commitment; no enacted fiscal rules or institutional reform evidence in passage |
| **D0015** | 7B | 7B.5, 7B.9 | The source notes López Obrador combined political and social progressivism with a more conservative approach on abortion and same-sex marriage, which he addressed with avoidance or ambiguity. | negative | `extracted HTML block 6` segment S00006 | direct fit: character note relevant to entire period | Behavioral observation; does not constitute evidence of enacted policy or institutional effect either way |
